title: 2026 Chinese jewellery retailer insights: Confidence check
gist: World Gold Council's 2026 survey of 744 Chinese jewellery retailers finds H1 tonnage the weakest since 2006 (136t) but value up 5% to RMB144bn, with investment demand (342t) outpacing jewellery, self-purchase now the main driver, lighter products rising, and retailers viewing weakness as delayed, not lost, demand.

insights.claim: In H1 2026 Chinese investors bought 342t of gold versus 136t of jewellery consumption, the weakest first half for jewellery since 2006, extending 2025 when investment demand first outpaced jewellery.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Chinese gold demand is now an investment/safe-haven story; jewellery volumes are cyclically depressed.

insights.claim: Falling domestic rates, a subdued property sector, weak consumer confidence and near-record precautionary savings pushed households into gold as a store of value, while the additional VAT burden introduced in late 2025 suppressed jewellery.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Chinese household safe-haven demand supports gold investment flows while property stays weak.

insights.claim: Under the VAT policy from November 2025, gold investment products sold via non-member channels bear roughly 13% additional tax, so franchisee jewellers scaled down or gave up bullion sales.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Policy has shifted bullion distribution away from jewellery retailers toward member channels.

insights.claim: High-tech manufacturing contributed 40% of China's y/y GDP growth in H1 2026 and the 'three new' sectors are over 18% of GDP, which WGC says points to an eventual recovery-phase confidence rebound.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Macro rotation could revive discretionary gold jewellery demand later.

insights.claim: H1 2026 gold jewellery consumption value rose 5% y/y to RMB144bn, the second-highest first half ever, despite a 30% y/y drop in tonnage, as consumers bought lighter pieces with fixed budgets.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Elevated price compresses volume but not spend; tonnage data overstates demand weakness.
insights.locator: Heritage and Hard Pure gold products continued to support sales

insights.claim: Heritage and Hard Pure gold outperformed for the fourth straight year, with 15% of retailers reporting higher Heritage sales and 12% higher Hard Pure sales in H1, while most categories contracted.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Differentiated 24K and cultural designs are the resilient niche.
insights.locator: Heritage and Hard Pure gold products continued to support sales

insights.claim: Lightweighting is now structural: more than 40% of retailers plan more sub-5g products and 47% more 5-10g, yet 62% also plan to expand higher labour-charge products, showing market polarisation.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Margin shifts toward design-heavy products; commodity gold weight matters less.

insights.claim: 44% of retailers say self-wear buying is essential to sales versus wedding purchases at 17%, up from 27% self-indulgent in 2024 and 37% in 2025 and down from 24% for weddings in 2024.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Jewellery demand is becoming more cyclical because self-purchase tracks confidence.
insights.quote: this self-indulgent purchasing accounted for 27% of total gold jewellery buying in 2024 and rose to 37% in 2025

insights.claim: Hard Pure gold buyers are younger, and Gen-Z consumers split spending into separate emotional-value and long-term-security accounts per Accenture's 2026 Chinese Consumer Insights.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Younger cohorts blend wealth preservation and self-expression.
insights.locator: Hard Pure gold consumers are younger

insights.claim: 45% of retailers plan to reduce gold inventory, the third year running that reducers exceed expanders, but over 40% plan no change, which WGC reads as cautious recalibration rather than retreat.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Passive destocking implies a rebound in orders when sentiment turns.

insights.claim: More than 60% of retailers believe consumers have postponed rather than abandoned purchases amid the gold price rally, and WGC's lagged-correlation analysis shows price spikes depress same-quarter demand but the effect fades and sustained strength may eventually support demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold price spikes cause temporary, not permanent, jewellery demand destruction in China.
insights.locator: Confidence check: retailers remain confident in gold

insights.claim: WGC concludes China's gold jewellery industry is recalibrating, not collapsing, with the structural repositioning from ceremonial to self-expression more consequential than any single price cycle.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Long-term demand composition is changing; track self-purchase share.
insights.quote: China's gold jewellery industry is not collapsing; rather, it is recalibrating.
